translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong ascended the throne he was posthumously enfeoffed Prince Sui and granted Grand Commander of Jing.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫得天下而治者，其道舒而有變；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: One who obtains the realm and governs it—his Way expands and has change;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: One who obtains the realm and governs it—his Way expands and admits change;

sentences.zh: 讓天下而退者，其道卷而常存。

translations.literal: one who yields the realm and withdraws—his Way rolls up yet constantly endures.
translations.idiomatic: one who yields the realm and withdraws—his Way rolls up yet constantly endures.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 飛龍在天，舒也；

translations.literal: The flying dragon in heaven—expansion;
translations.idiomatic: The flying dragon in heaven—that is expansion;

sentences.zh: 亢龍有悔，變也。

translations.literal: the proud dragon has regret—change.
translations.idiomatic: the proud dragon has regret—that is change.

sentences.zh: 讓皇帝守無咎於或躍，利終吉於勞謙，其用有光，其聞莫朽。

translations.literal: The Emperor Who Yielded kept himself without blame at "perhaps leaping," and gained ultimate good fortune in "laborious modesty"; his use had brilliance, and his fame will not decay.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor Who Yielded kept himself without blame at "perhaps leaping," and gained ultimate good fortune in "laborious modesty"; his conduct shone, and his fame will not decay.

sentences.zh: 惠莊、惠文、惠宣、隋王等，或守常而獲免，終保皇枝；

translations.literal: Crown Prince Hui Zhuang, Crown Prince Hui Wen, Crown Prince Hui Xuan, Prince Sui, and the like—some by keeping to the constant obtained exemption and in the end preserved the imperial branch;
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Hui Zhuang, Crown Prince Hui Wen, Crown Prince Hui Xuan, Prince Sui, and the like—some, by keeping to the constant, obtained exemption and in the end preserved the imperial branch;

sentences.zh: 或過望而包羞，竟塵青史。

translations.literal: some by overreaching brought shame upon themselves and in the end stained the blue history.
translations.idiomatic: some, by overreaching, brought shame upon themselves and in the end stained the historical record.

sentences.zh: 略陽公信魁偉之狀，起圖謀之心，福善禍淫，宜哉不令。

translations.literal: Duke of Lueyang Zhen trusted his grand and imposing appearance and raised a heart of plotting; fortune favors the good and calamity follows the evil—fitting indeed that he did not end well.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Lueyang Zhen trusted his grand and imposing appearance and raised a heart of plotting; fortune favors the good and calamity follows the evil—fitting indeed that he did not end well.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：謙而受益，讓以成賢。

translations.literal: In praise it is said: Through modesty one benefits; through yielding one becomes worthy.
translations.idiomatic: In praise it is said: Through modesty one benefits; through yielding one becomes worthy.

sentences.zh: 唐屬之美，憲得其先。

translations.literal: Among the beauties of the Tang house, Xian obtained the first place.
translations.idiomatic: Among the beauties of the Tang house, Xian obtained the first place.

sentences.zh: 長不居震，剛不乘乾。

translations.literal: The eldest does not occupy the thunder trigram; the firm does not ride the qian trigram.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest does not occupy the thunder trigram; the firm does not ride the qian trigram.

sentences.zh: 讓之大者，胡可比焉。

translations.literal: In yielding at its greatest—how can it be compared?
translations.idiomatic: In yielding at its greatest—how can any other be compared?

sentences.zh: 捴、範已降，同氣連枝。

translations.literal: From Cui and Fan downward, they shared one breath and linked branches.
translations.idiomatic: From Cui and Fan downward, they shared one breath and linked branches.

sentences.zh: 性習何遠，非革即睽。

translations.literal: How far apart are nature and habit—if not reformed, then estranged.
translations.idiomatic: How far apart are nature and habit—if not reformed, then estranged.

sentences.zh: 有善有惡，禍福不欺。

translations.literal: There is good and there is evil; fortune and calamity do not deceive.
translations.idiomatic: There is good and there is evil; fortune and calamity do not deceive.
